description: Shared Linear Relations candidate inventory. Mathematical questions are stored independently from curriculum-specific standards and mapped separately to each supported curriculum.

questions.learning_goal: Solve a pair of simultaneous linear equations graphically.
questions.proposed_design: Give the learner two linear equations. For each equation, the learner constructs its graph using two draggable points. After both lines are constructed, the learner reports the ordered pair where the two graphs intersect. This makes QLIN-10 procedural and materially harder than QLIN-08, where the graphs were already supplied.

questions.learning_goal: Complete tables, graph two relations, identify their intersection, and state the simultaneous-equation solution.

acquisition_decision.reason: QLIN-12 is intended as an integrated mastery task. No single verified source covers the full required table-to-graph-to-intersection-to-solution progression, so the design combines verified open components and extends them into one curriculum-independent mastery activity.

student_flow: complete missing values in two linear-relation tables
use the completed values to construct both linear graphs
state the ordered-pair solution of the simultaneous equations
diagnostic_targets: wrong linear relation used while completing a table
duplicate graph points that do not define a line
graph A and graph B swapped
graph inconsistent with the completed table
proposed_design.assessment_distinction: QLIN-11 assesses contextual modelling from relationships to equations, graphs, and interpretation. QLIN-12 instead integrates the full curriculum progression from tables to graph construction to intersection to the final simultaneous-equation solution.
